name: Elton Lock

layers.essential_history: [[c:This is the River Nene. For centuries Elton people crossed it at a ford, until a wooden bridge was built in 1844 and a stone one in 1875. Look out for boats working through the lock.]]
layers.deeper_history: [[c:The Nene runs from Northamptonshire to the Wash. The locks let boats climb and fall between stretches of the river.]]
layers.mystery: [[c:Long before the lock and the bridges, people crossed the Nene here at a ford. Ned Cobb kept the crossing and wrote down everyone he helped across. He hands you his ledger.]]

sources.title: Elton Parish Council: A short history of Elton

directions_to_next: [[c:Head east, about 240 metres as the crow flies, to Elton Methodist Church. Head back up River Lane and turn right along Middle Street. Keep to the pavements and paths.]]

puzzle.title: [[c:The ford-keeper's ledger]]
material: [[c:Ten o'clock: Mistress Carey, to the church side.]]
[[c:Eleven o'clock: Master Hale, to the far bank, with a bundle.]]
[[c:Midnight: Master Hale, back again, hands empty.]]
[[c:One o'clock: Thomas Wade, home from the inn.]]
puzzle.question: [[c:Who crossed the ford twice? (surname)]]
puzzle.reveal: [[c:Master Hale crossed twice, carrying a bundle one way and nothing the other, even though he told everyone he never left the inn.]]

evidence: [[c:Master Hale crossed the ford twice that night, though he said he never left the inn.]]
